title.narrative: Integrated Cholera Prevention and Emergency Health Response in High-Risk Areas of Gambella Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThis action is designed in response to the EHF’s 2025 1st reserve allocation call and aims to address the humanitarian needs of 80247 (40926 female) cholera-affected/at-risk people living infour cholera-impacted woredas in Gambella region. It is co-designed and jointly implemented by ZOA (consortium lead and WASH sector specialist) and Nexus Ethiopia (local NGO, sub-applicant and Health sector specialist), and provides critical WASH and health services. The action follows a holistic, integrated, and complementary approach that leverages the expertise, resources and local experience of partners, grassroots community and government structures. During the project design and project cycle management phases, ZOA and Nexus Ethiopia will follow a common approach of joint planning, implementation and monitoring, targeting the same people, at the same time, in the same place, based on common objectives and shared analysis of needs and priorities. WASH: The WASH intervention focuses on increasing targeted beneficiaries' access to safe and clean water at community and institution level through: rehabilitation of nonfunctional water schemes connecting pipelines to health facilities (especially those providing cholera treatment services) construction of temporary latrines a in Cholera Treatment Centers (CTC), construction of handwashing facilities in CTCs and schools and enhanced sanitation and hygiene awareness in targeted communities to deliver behavioral and practice changes, to reduce water borne diseases and contribute to improved health outcomes. The WASH actions will reach a total of 33,762 people ( 17219 female). Health: this project will establish and enhance CTCs and Cholera Treatment Units (CTUs) through distribution of Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) supplies, strengthen government health experts’ ability to handle cholera case management, and fulfil logistical gaps/covering overtime to ensure the provision of 24/7 CTC service delivery. Community outreach activities, community health awareness, case detection and referral system interventions will be implemented. The health actions will reach 16156 people ( 7820 females).ltbrgtltbrgtThe project places protection at its core and ensures meaningful engagement of communities and stakeholders throughout implementation, and ensures safe, dignified and inclusive service to vulnerable community members. Context-appropriate Complaint, Feedback, and Response Mechanisms (CFRM) will be established to amplify voices, address concerns, and improve accountability. To prevent duplication of resources/efforts and maximize the project impact, ZOA and Nexus Ethiopia will coordinate with humanitarian partners (i.e. MSF-H and DPO) who are active in the cholera response across the target woredas. The project will build on ZOA’s ongoing ECHO-RRM funded cholera response and ensure complementarity.ltbrgtlt/pgt
